title: The Fall of Constantinople
description: April-May 1453. The player commands the last defenders of Byzantium under Constantine XI. Hold the Theodosian Walls against Mehmed II's siege: repair breaches from bombard fire, guard the sea walls along the Golden Horn, and survive repeated assaults. Defeat comes if the Hagia Sophia district falls; victory means holding until the final assault is broken.

anachronisms_found: RICHARD_THE_LIONHEART placed as the player's hero: an English king who died in 1199, standing in for Constantine XI Palaiologos (d. 1453) — a 250-year error, and the engine offers Byzantine-flavoured alternatives (e.g. Belisarius, Theodore Lascaris) or at minimum a renamed generic unit

SALADIN placed as the enemy commander: the Ayyubid sultan of the Third Crusade era, used to represent Mehmed II; the dialogue calls him 'Mehmed II' while the placed object is an unambiguously 12th-century Kurdish/Egyptian hero
TREE_PALM_FOREST x20 as the map's only vegetation — palm forest is desert/tropical terrain, wholly wrong for Thrace and the Bosphorus, where pine/oak/Mediterranean tree sets are available

No gunpowder siege whatsoever among placed objects, despite the brief promising 'repair breaches from bombard fire'; the engine has Bombard Cannons and Great Bombards (the Ottoman signature weapon of 1453)
Free-standing GOLD_MINE x11, STONE_MINE x4, FORAGE_BUSH x8 and SHEEP inside/around a besieged imperial capital — random-map economic furniture, not a walled metropolis under blockade
